stories.description: Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost to incumbent Lula in Sunday's presidential election, has reportedly fled the country. Bolsonaro, who is facing multiple corruption probes, has refused to concede.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel election: Anti-Netanyahu bloc ahead, but no majority
stories.description: While Netanyahu's party is projected to be the biggest in parliament, the anti-Netanyahu coalition looks set to have more seats. But no bloc has a clear majority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel election: Exit polls show no clear winner, with Netanyahu's fate unclear
stories.description: While Netanyahu's party is projected to be the biggest in parliament, two out of three exit polls show his bloc even with the opposition. No bloc has a clear majority. DW has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU proposes giving Frontex border agency new major powers
stories.description: The European Commission has unveiled a new plan to give Frontex more resources to ensure the return of irregular migrants, including by supporting non-EU countries. The move comes after the tragedy in Ceuta.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Mbappe apologizes as Chinese sponsors drop him and TV broadcasts are halted over Mao dictator remark
stories.description: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe has apologized after apparently referring to Mao Zedong as a dictator. Chinese sponsors have dropped him, while state television has suspended Spanish league broadcasts.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Myanmar: Is the US undermining the EU's diplomatic blockade?
stories.description: With the US reopening talks with Myanmar's military-backed government, and several Southeast Asian countries restarting diplomatic contacts, the EU is facing uncomfortable questions about its own boycott of the junta.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Turnout at Israel's election has reached a record high at the halfway stage
stories.description: Almost 45% of the electorate had voted by 2 p.m., the highest share since such records began in 1973. The highly anticipated vote is expected to be a close-fought contest, and perhaps even a stalemate.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
stories.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Will Israel elections change its Iran approach?
stories.description: As Israelis head to the polls, the country's conflict with Iran casts a long shadow over the ballot box. But any leadership changes in Israel may not be enough to shake up its grand strategy on Tehran.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Will elections in Israel change its Iran approach?
stories.description: As Israelis head to the polls, the country's conflict with Iran casts a long shadow over the ballot box. But any leadership changes in Israel may not be enough to shake up its grand strategy on Tehran.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Denmark's Frederiksen criticizes Finland and Norway for calling Putin without coordinating with allies, despite consultation with Ukraine
stories.description: Finland and Norway have called Putin about ending the Ukraine war, drawing Danish criticism. The dispute highlights divisions over European engagement with Moscow ahead of planned US-led peace talks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jordan acknowledges civilian casualties in Syria airstrike against 'Islamic State'
stories.description: A Jordanian government spokesman has expressed "regret" over civilian casualties in an airstrike it said was targeting "IS" militants.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: DR Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases as the outbreak spreads abroad, with no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo virus
stories.description: DR Congo has reported more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths. The outbreak involves a virus for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, complicating efforts to contain its spread.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
stories.description: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Two men face UK national security charges following an incident near RAF Fairford, with police suspecting Iranian state involvement
stories.description: British prosecutors have charged two men over an incident near RAF Fairford in September. Police suspect Iranian involvement in the case at a base used for US strikes on Iran.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Police in northern Germany search for suspects after car ramming overnight injures several
stories.description: A person intentionally drove into a group of people in a northern German town, police have said. The suspects fled on foot and remain at large.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: India news: Arunachal sees fresh violence over proposed dam
stories.description: More violence erupted in India's northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh over proposed hydroelectric projects that locals are protesting. Also, India's top court will hear pleas against the poll body chief. More on DW.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Israel election: Israelis vote for 1st time since October 7 terror attack
stories.description: Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, faces a battle to stay in power amid fierce competition from a bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties are projected to play kingmakers.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Brazil elections: Merz, world leaders congratulate Lula on his win
stories.description: Brazilian President Lula secured a surprise win over far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, whose party recognizes Lula's election victory.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia begin Oleshky ceasefire for aid mission
stories.description: Around 2,000 people remain stranded in the city of Oleshky, facing severe shortages of food and medicine. The Russian-occupied town has been devastated by fighting and flooding since Moscow's invasion in 2022.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US seeks new charges against former FBI chief James Comey
stories.description: The Trump administration accuses the former FBI director of leaking classified information a decade ago. Comey denies wrongdoing, while his lawyers argue the case is legally invalid and comes too late.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
stories.description: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jordan says its military struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after deadly church attack
stories.description: Jordanian armed forces carried out strikes on "militant hideouts" in Syria that it said were linked to a deadly church attack on the kingdom last week. Syria gave a different account.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UN sounds the alarm over Israel's West Bank military operation
stories.description: The UN has sounded the alarm on Israeli action in the West Bank city of Hebron after hundreds of families were displaced at the weekend. Israel has ordered the military to demolish homes after soldiers were killed there.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: A bad omen? Syria bans women from university courses
stories.description: The recent announcement that Syrian tertiary institutes will not allow women into some courses has triggered debate. Critics worry it may be a sign that the new Syrian government is restricting women's rights.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: AI company Anthropic files its IPO in hopes of raising $100 billion
stories.description: Anthropic has filed paperwork for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest in history. The company has yet to turn a profit.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: German police probe cruise ship captain after Bremerhaven collision
stories.description: A three-ship collision has led to the cancellation of a cruise and expensive damages. Shipyard repairs are needed, and further cruises could be affected.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
stories.description: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Why Ukraine may be involved in Mali's conflict
stories.description: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Macron vows 'strong measures' to combat protests that rocked France
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said his government will announce "strong measures" in response to violent protests in France in recent weeks. But he also acknowledged that students have "legitimate" grievances.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany's Merz heads to Asia as security issues loom large
stories.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will be meeting the leaders of Singapore, Japan and South Korea as Germany seeks to adjust its foreign policy to rising uncertainty and threats to global supply chains.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
stories.description: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region, but also wants good ties with Beijing.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Jordan: 3 arrested over deadly church attack
stories.description: Three men have been arrested in Jordan in connection with an attack on a Greek Orthodox church last week. The arrests took place following a dawn shootout with security forces during which the suspects were wounded.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany news: Union slams Audi CEO for joining Trump at campaign rally, while Chancellor Merz and President Steinmeier embark on separate Asia tours
stories.description: Audi's boss is facing a backlash in Germany after appearing alongside Donald Trump at a campaign rally. Meanwhile, Germany's chancellor and president are heading to Asia on separate diplomatic missions. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany news: Audi boss slammed over Trump rally appearance
stories.description: Audi's boss is facing a backlash in Germany after appearing alongside Donald Trump at a campaign rally. Meanwhile, Germany's chancellor and president are heading to Asia on separate diplomatic missions. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Venezuela: Opposition leader Machado returns from exile, received by thousands of supporters in Caracas
stories.description: Nobel Peach Prize winner and popular Venezuelan political opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned from nearly a year in exile. She was greeted by thousands of cheering supporters in Caracas.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Venezuelan opposition leader Machado returns from exile
stories.description: Nobel Peace Prize winner and popular Venezuelan political opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned after nearly a year away. She was greeted by thousands of cheering supporters in Caracas.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: India news: Remark on Modi's father stirs political row
stories.description: An opposition leader's impromptu remark concerning PM Modi is causing a political stir in India with the ruling party now planning a protest. Also, the prince of Liechtenstein is in Mumbai. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Brazilian leftist President Lula wins reelection against conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro
stories.description: Leftist President Lula has defeated right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro to win another term in office. Bolsonaro has refused to concede and called for the results to be annulled. DW has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Brazil elections: Vote counting resumes after extension
stories.description: Votes are being tallied after polling was extended two more hours. The result between leftist Lula and right-wing Bolsonaro is expected to be very close. DW has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Serbia election: Vucic concedes defeat to student-led movement
stories.description: In a seismic political shift, Serbia's longtime strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic has conceded defeat to a student-led movement in the country's parliamentary elections.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Protein shakes for teenagers: Good or bad idea?
stories.description: Protein products are marketed as a way of building muscle and losing weight — and they're very popular with young people. They also claim to promote healthy growth in children. Is this true? How much protein is healthy?
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Brazil election: Lula, Bolsonaro cast votes in final bout
stories.description: Almost 160 million are eligible to vote in the final round of Brazil's election that pits the left-wing incumbent against the son of the former far-right president. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Brazil elections: Voting extended after transport complaints
stories.description: Supporters of left-wing Lula and far-right Bolsonaro have two more hours to vote after polling was extended. The result is expected to be very close. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
stories.description: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel to close all West Bank land crossings on election day
stories.description: After a deadly attack which killed two Israeli soldiers on Friday, the Israeli military has said all land border points between Israel and the occupied West Bank will be closed during Tuesday's election.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany news: Fire flares up at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat
stories.description: Fire broke out again overnight at a former mountain retreat used by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler. Meanwhile, a survey shows most people in Germany feel the days of the governing coalition are numbered. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
stories.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Brazil votes in tight runoff between leftist Lula and right-wing Flavio Bolsonaro
stories.description: The high stakes election will decide whether Brazil will move toward the right or retain a leftist government.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: India news: Rahul Gandhi urges protest against voter deletions, announces November 1 rally
stories.description: India's opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has accused the ruling BJP of "vote theft" and urged people to join a rally in Delhi on November 1. The call comes amid protests over revision of electoral rolls. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Serbia votes in closely fought election as student-led opposition challenges Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power
stories.description: Nearly two years after a deadly railway station collapse sparked mass anti-corruption protests, Serbians are voting in a closely fought election that could end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Serbia election: Can student-led opposition end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power?
stories.description: Nearly two years after a deadly railway station collapse sparked mass anti-corruption protests, Serbians are voting in a closely fought election that could end Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Serbia election: Student-led opposition ends Aleksandar Vucic's grip on power
stories.description: In a seismic political shift, Serbia’s longtime strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led movement in the country's parliamentary elections.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot campaigns on Moroccan roots in challenge to Netanyahu
stories.description: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Prague honours Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
stories.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
stories.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Saudi Arabia looks to US for an AI edge as Yemen's Houthis up pressure
stories.description: The US is helping Saudi Arabia fight the Houthi group in Yemen with AI-assisted targeting. But AI is not a magic bullet, experts say, and there are technological, political and human rights issues to consider.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
stories.description: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
stories.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Serbia election: Student movement seeks to end Aleksandar Vucic's rule
stories.description: After two years of student-led, anti-corruption protests, Serbia is holding an early parliamentary election that could break long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vucic's grip on the Balkan country.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion factory in US
stories.description: After Donald Trump made the announcement at an election rally in Georgia, the German carmaker confirmed plans for a factory in the US state, but noted car production would only start early next decade.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to sex abuse survivors
stories.description: Around 1,300 survivors agreed to the $800 million payout from the Catholic Church, marking one of the largest clergy abuse settlements in the US.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu launches reelection bid amid economic woes
stories.description: President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine: Starlink satellite speeds restored to normal
stories.description: The announcement comes after Starlink and Starshield restrictions had disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: German national facing trial for alleged attempt to join IS
stories.description: A 21-year-old suspect is being held in pre-trial detention for allegedly trying to join the "Islamic State" terror group.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
stories.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Will Guinea-Bissau remain trapped in political chaos?
stories.description: Elections scheduled for December 6 in Guinea-Bissau have been postponed indefinitely. No new date has been set, leaving the country's return to civilian rule uncertain.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
stories.description: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Germany news: Merz calls for unity at CSU party conference
stories.description: With his coalition under pressure, Merz delivered an address at the close of the CSU conference in Munich. Meanwhile, fire has largely destroyed Hitler's former Eagle's Nest retreat. DW has more
stories.subject: World

stories.title: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travels to Chinese border city via newly opened bridge
stories.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un travelled to China’s border city of Dandong via a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, where he met a senior Chinese official.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France protests: More violence feared amid renewed demonstrations
stories.description: France is deploying some 70,000 police as fresh nationwide protests are set to begin. A deadly shooting near Paris has additionally fueled tensions. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
stories.description: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France: Clashes break out as protests go nationwide
stories.description: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as tens of thousands participate in a new round of protests. The situation is slowing turning tense in some cities like Paris and Marseille. Follow DW.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Why Russia's arrest of Japanese journalist is the latest sign of deteriorating ties between the countries.
stories.description: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Taiwan: Typhoon Champi leaves 1 dead, over 500 injured
stories.description: After killing one person and causing major disruptions in Taiwan, Typhoon Champi is now headed towards China.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: India news: India-China border tensions back in focus despite ongoing talks
stories.description: India says Chinese forces deviating from established patrolling patterns continue to disrupt the border situation, a day after the ITBP chief reported face-offs at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: India news: Neha Bora refuses to sign peace bond, cites right to democratic dissent
stories.description: Neha Bora says the peace bond violates the right to democratic dissent. The statement comes amid a wider protest calling for the removal of India's election chief. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: India news: Andhra, Odisha brace for severe storm
stories.description: The weather department warned that a depression over the Bay of Bengal could escalate into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast, with winds reaching 140 km/h. DW has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat catches fire, police say
stories.description: Authorities have arrested a suspect as firemen try to put out the fire in Bavaria, near the Austrian border.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France to deploy 70,000 police officers ahead of protests
stories.description: With new protests in France planned for this weekend, the authorities pledged to do everything in their power to prevent looting, violence and vandalism.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Ebola: Kenya announces second death
stories.description: Kenyan health officials said the 65-year-old ​woman was a close ‌relative of a ‌​man who died of Ebola last month. The woman developed symptoms ‌while under quarantine in Nairobi.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
stories.description: The move comes as Trump's Republican Party scrambles to maintain control of the US Congress, with a Republican candidate in a key Senate race saying she had lobbied to lift the tariffs on Canadian products.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
stories.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured
stories.description: A shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan happened during a funeral, according to authorities. Two unidentified men opened fire on the procession, with Jordan's king vowing "the harshest retaliation."
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
stories.description: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky, occupied by Russia and on the frontline, faces a humanitarian crisis. The localized truce comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said negotiators would meet for wider talks next month.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: November 13 Paris attacks: Eleven years later, France pays tribute to victims
stories.description: Eleven years on, France pays tribute to the victims of the November 13 attacks. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered this Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
stories.description: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
stories.description: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area. Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
stories.description: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
stories.description: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. "Without the support of financial entities, of insurance, of providing goods and so on, settlements, big settlements, would not exist," he argues.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
stories.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France asks Brussels to examine Algeria's non-compliance of EU association agreement
stories.description: France announced on Friday that it will ask the European Commission to "examine" Algeria's non-compliance with its EU association agreement. Earlier in July, Algiers imposed a near-blanket ban on French imports, and last month, Algeria suspended urea shipments to France.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Nvidia scandal: How close was ex-CEO to Trump?
stories.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Just how close Huang was to Trump and the extent of the influence tech giants have on his administration are some of the questions that still need answering, says France 24’s Douglas Herbert.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russia strikes targets across Ukraine as Kyiv launches nearly 1,200 drones
stories.description: Russian strikes hit targets across Ukraine on Thursday, with one attack damaging a hospital. Ukraine meanwhile fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Haitian forces recapture national stadium after two years of gang control
stories.description: Haitian security forces regained control Thursday, November 12, of the country's main stadium that had been under gang control for two years, forcing the national football team to play elsewhere. The Haitian National Police said in a statement that it had taken "full control" of the venue with the Task Force, a private security group serving the government, after which it left the stadium under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Roger Waters launches heartfelt plea for 'an end to the genocide in Gaza'
stories.description: Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has always mixed art with activism. A long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause, the star guitarist has now released a re-imagined version of the rock anthem "Comfortably Numb" with Palestinian American singer Mona Miari singing in Arabic. He tells FRANCE 24's Lyana Saleh why proceeds of the record are going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund and why he can never become "Comfortably Numb" with the violence and suffering in Gaza.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
stories.description: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".
stories.subject: World

stories.title: The truth about Douma: How Syria covered up a chemical attack
stories.description: On April 7, 2018, the Syrian town of Douma, on the outskirts of the capital Damascus, was targeted by a chemical attack. Evidence pointed to the Syrian regime, yet proof vanished, and eyewitnesses went silent. Eight years later, FRANCE 24's Jenna Le Bras tracked down survivors and witnesses of the deadly attack. She also met representatives of some of the world's most powerful institutions to understand how a massive cover-up campaign had been orchestrated by the regime, with Russian support.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: What does the 'Blue Tsunami' mean for US media?
stories.description: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop looks at the impact of the midterm elections in the United States. While the results are being reckoned with by Republicans and celebrated by Democrats, what does it all mean for the press? Some media analysts wonder whether certain outlets, particularly ones accused of being cosy with the Trump administration, will change their tone. Our guest this week is International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Most Ukrainians 'think there's no chance of a peace deal' with Russia
stories.description: Ukrainian attacks killed at least nine people in Russia overnight, while Moscow struck a hospital in Kyiv and killed at least three in the south of the country, officials on both sides said Friday. It comes a day after intense shuttle diplomacy in US-led talks to end the war approaching its fifth year but, says France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg, most people in Ukraine think there is "no chance" of a peace deal being reached.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'A lot of emotion' as Paris marks 11 years since terror attacks
stories.description: France on Friday marked 11 years since the November 13, 2015, terror attacks that left more than 130 dead in the capital. France 24's James André reports from outside the Bataclan concert venue, one of the sites targeted in the attacks, where he says there was "a lot of emotion" as homage was paid to the victims.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 🔴 Live: Microsoft reports 'improvements' to Outlook services in North America, Europe
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: UK rocked by comedians' sex scandals
stories.description: The UK is facing a reckoning in the world of entertainment, as two well-known comedy figures find themselves at the centre of serious allegations and headlines. This as Russell Brand is jailed for more than 10 years after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault and David Walliams faces serious allegations of sexual misconduct.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: The scourge of femicide in Mexico: Impunity reigns in state of Morelos
stories.description: When Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president in 2024, she pledged to tackle violence against women. And while femicides have fallen since she took office, the numbers remain alarming, with around 520 murders so far this year. In the small state of Morelos, just outside the capital Mexico City, four female students have been murdered since January, including a Spanish woman on an exchange programme. The state has one of the highest femicide rates in the country.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Ukraine’s mobilisation methods spark criticism
stories.description: Social media in Ukraine is full of videos showing suspected cases of forced mobilisation. Such incidents are known as “busification”, as the recruitment officers typically take the conscripts away in minibuses. The videos have been fuelling growing opposition to the recruitment practices.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nvidia scandal: Was Alice Huang really a Chinese spy?
stories.description: It is another twist in the downfall of Jensen Huang, CEO of AI chip giant Nvidia, who resigned on Thursday. The US Justice Department says it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman he had an affair with, was a spy. CNN is also reporting sources from across the US intelligence community who say there is no definitive proof she was an intelligence asset for Beijing
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: It's 'game over' for Jensen Huang, king of AI chips
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 13: We look at reactions to the resignation of Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia. It comes in the wake of multiple affairs he allegedly had, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. What are the repercussions for the AI industry and for AI trade relations? Also: France's Les Bleus lose to Italy in the Nations League, marking Zinédine Zidane's first defeat as coach. Plus: a raccoon that went viral for getting drunk last year ends up raising a lot of money for an animal shelter!
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
stories.description: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium on Thursday, ending two years of gang control. Salvadoran troops have now taken over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush in which four of its troops went missing.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: US, Ukraine say Europe to join peace talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance
stories.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday, November 12, Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war. In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Zelensky in Dublin.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Who will inherit 007's licence to thrill? 'The world is not enough' in the hunt for James Bond
stories.description: More than six decades after James Bond first appeared on the big screen, the search for Daniel Craig's successor has become a revealing debate about the future of one of cinema's most enduring, and endearing, franchises. "From the cold-blooded sexual magnetism of Sean Connery to the more tongue-in-cheek take of Roger Moore, to Daniel Craig's gritty realism, there's really a James Bond for everyone." But who will inherit the licence to thrill? FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes us on this exciting edge-of-your-seat adventure with a "view to a kill". Should Bond remain faithful to his traditional identity, or reinvent himself to reflect changing attitudes towards gender, diversity and contemporary heroism?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 2027 AFCON Qualifiers: Top guns Senegal, Cameroon, Ivory Coast deliver
stories.description: Africa's heavyweights are delivering in the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. Senegal marked Patrick Vieira's first home game with an emphatic win over Sudan, while Cameroon and Ivory Coast took further steps towards qualification.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV meets abuse victims in Peru, says Church must make 'amends'
stories.description: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, including people linked to the disbanded Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pontiff also urged the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served for nearly two decades.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Haitian police retake national stadium from gangs after two years
stories.description: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium on Thursday after two years under gang control, with Salvadoran troops taking over security at the venue. The operation comes as El Salvador deploys 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush that left four of its troops missing.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Live: Zelensky and Kushner confirm that Europe will join next round of Russia-Ukraine talks
stories.description: US envoy and President ​Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on Thursday Russia and ​Ukraine ‌agreed ⁠to expand the next ‌round of talks to include ⁠European nations, who will debate whether their envoy should be one individual or more and who should represent them at a summit in Dublin on Friday. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Peruvian pope’ Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a Pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarized nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: ‘Peruvian pope’ Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a Pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarized nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone. His decades of pastoral experience in Peru, amid political instability, terrorism, state violence and profound social inequalities, have shaped a religious outlook rooted in cultural openness, solidarity with the marginalized and an intimate understanding of human suffering.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Eight killed, including two children, in New York building collapse
stories.description: Eight people, including two children, were killed when a residential building collapsed into an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn on Wednesday. Firefighters spent hours searching the rubble overnight before declaring the operation over on Thursday, as authorities launched an investigation into the disaster.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russia using 'illegal and unethical means, knows Europe won't use same means back', expert says
stories.description: There are mounting concerns across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks could be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Elisabeth Braw, Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative. She says that Russia's aim is to "increase its power at the expense of European countries and the easiest way to do that is to constantly wage this dirty war against European countries, using illegal and unethical means, because Russia knows that we are not going to use the same means back".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russia using 'illegal and unethical means, knows Europe won't use same means back', expert says
stories.description: There are mounting concern across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks could be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Elisabeth Braw, Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative. She says that Russia's aim is to "increase its power at the expense of European countries and the easiest way to do that is to constantly wage this dirty war against European countries, using illegal and unethical means, because Russia knows that we are not going to use the same means back".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after mounting scandals
stories.description: Jensen Huang, long considered the face of the AI revolution, has resigned as Nvidia's President, CEO and board member as sandals over his romantic affairs wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the company's market value in a matter of days. US lawmakers signal they'll likely push for tighter export restrictions for AI chips. Meanwhile, the rapid buildout of AI data centre is sparking anger and worries among French communities.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Mauritania fishing boats falsely portrayed as migrant fleet bound for Spain
stories.description: Spain’s Canary Islands are facing renewed pressure from migrant arrivals, with local authorities declaring a state of emergency. Against this backdrop, a viral video claims to show thousands of boats in Mauritania amassing at the port, that users said was "ready to set sail" to carry migrants to the archipelago. But the satellite images are misleading: they show a traditional fishing port, not a fleet of migrant vessels. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
stories.description: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. And music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ngo criticizes UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
stories.description: In tonight's edition, Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. And a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'There's no such thing as safe' in contact sports, brain injury expert says
stories.description: Discussing the issue of contact sports and the threat to sports men and women of all ages, particularly in the light of the recent death, just last month, of a 17-year-old French woman after a head collision on the rugby field, FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Daniel H Daneshvar, Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School. He says that "there's not such thing as safe" in contact sports, explaining that "if you get a lot of repeated hits to the head, then you're at risk for problems later in life, both in the near term and the long term".
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, including surgeon, medics say
stories.description: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of them in the bombing of Nasser hospital in south Gaza early in the day, health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Goher Rahbour, a surgeon working at the Nasser Hospital.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Zelensky warns Europe over US-Russia talks on broader security arrangements
stories.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders Thursday to be wary of discussions between the United States and Russia about a new security arrangement for the continent. Before launching the war in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO on Europe's security arrangements which included demands for the alliance to withdraw forces from eastern Europe and stop accepting new members. FRANCE 24's Caroline Baum reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Plugged-in planet? COP31 host Turkey leads charge for electrification
stories.description: It’s sweater weather in Paris. But even though November brings brisk temperatures and fall foliage, it doesn’t mean last summer’s record heat should fade from our memories. One of the suggested reasons why students are so boiling mad is the hell they endured back in June in overheated classrooms and baking shoebox apartments.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: White House reportedly discussing Howard Lutnick's future as Commerce secretary
stories.description: Senior White House officials are discussing whether ​Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out in the wake of the spy scandal surrounding Nvidia's now ​former ‌CEO Jensen Huang, two people familiar ⁠with the situation told Reuters on Thursday. In June, Reuters reported that the Trump administration had held ⁠off from adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to a trade blacklist. FRANCE 24's Wassim Cornet reports from Los Angeles.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Winter is coming: Putin seeks to 'hammer Ukrainians, their power grid, their water supplies'
stories.description: As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow American approach to mediation. For Russia expert Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. "The Russian approach is always to sound incredibly bullish and then make any concessions at the very last minute," he explains, suggesting that the Kremlin's uncompromising rhetoric should not necessarily be mistaken for an absolute refusal to negotiate. Yet the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to surrender territory it continues to hold. "That Donbas question is, for me, an intractable one," Galeotti observes, warning that neither side currently appears willing to cede territory necessary for a breakthrough. Whereas conventional diplomacy generally proceeds through discreet negotiations before culminating in political announcements, Trump's approach has effectively reversed that sequence. "Trump makes grand declarations and various people try desperately to make it happen."
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel to ban far-left French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entry
stories.description: The Israeli government said Thursday that it would ban far-left French leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entering the country after the French presidential contender said he would use French vessels to force aid into Gaza if he were elected. The announcement comes a day after France confirmed it had refused entry to the head of a body representing settlements in the occupied West Bank.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Labelled terrorists’: How France is using anti-terror powers to deter protests
stories.description: The French government has been accused of weaponising an anti-terror law adopted in the wake of the 2015 Paris attacks to keep dozens of people away from massive protests sweeping the country. Lawyers and rights groups denounce an abuse of power with potentially dangerous repercussions for individual liberties and the right to protest.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Concentration of power & wealth: Do tech CEOs have more authority, influence than elected officials?
stories.description: The resignation of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has thrown one of the world's most iconic technology companies into a leadership crisis, whose ripple effects extend far beyond Silicon Valley. Nvidia occupies a unique position in a booming AI industruy marked by intensifying competition between the United States and China. Its leadership upheaval raises immediate questions about corporate succession. But it is also fueling a broader debate about economic resilience, national security and the political influence of big tech titans. For Gavin Bade, trade and economic policy reporter at The Wall Street Journal, the controversy illustrates the extraordinary concentration of economic power in a handful of corporations and the individuals who lead them. “Do these CEOs actually have more authority and more influence than our elected officials?”
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Russia's Vladimir Putin suggests no Ukraine compromise in meeting with US envoys
stories.description: Russia's President Vladimir Putin indicated on Thursday, November 12, that the Kremlin would not compromise on its hardline demands to end the war in Ukraine, but offered a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city during a meeting with US envoys. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel kills six in Gaza hospital strike as 9-month-old baby freezes to death
stories.description: An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians Thursday, including a teenage boy and a surgeon, medics said. Elsewhere in the devastated Palestinian territory, a nine-month-old baby died from the cold as families flee worsening flooding.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: How FRANCE 24 traced Tehran-backed Afghan fighters from Syria to southeastern Iran
stories.description: Members of the Tehran-backed Afghan Shia militia known as the Fatemiyoun division have resurfaced in Iran after largely disappearing from public view following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria in 2024. FRANCE 24 used "martyrdom” announcements and the geolocation of videos shared on social media to trace their presence.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: At least five people shot in DC neighbourhood near the White House
stories.description: At least one person died after five people were shot early Thursday in a Washington, DC neighbourhood near the White House, police said. A swarm of officers responded to a nearby apartment building where a suspect was barricaded and later shot himself.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Life through a lens: Celebrating 200 years of photography
stories.description: A passport photo, a selfie, an award-winning film and even the evening news: all of them were made possible thanks to a "fantastic machine", the camera. As France celebrates the bicentenary of the first fixed photographic image, we discuss the image-obsessed society we live in with filmmaker Maximilien Van Aertryck and artist Alina Frieske.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded at war memorial
stories.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, along with his wife and aides, was silenced by a guard on Wednesday at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth's group was at Arlington National Cemetery for a Veterans Day ceremony when they were reprimanded for laughing and taking pictures in front of the sombre memorial.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations on extramarital affairs
stories.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Washington Fraser Jackson and FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert have more.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down
stories.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its leather-jacket-clad leader at a crucial time for the sector.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: European security and Ukraine talks top agenda at Dublin summit
stories.description: Leaders from more than 50 European countries and institutions are gathering in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, hosted by Ireland under the theme “Europe – strong, secure and connected”. The summit highlighted the need for Europe to have a seat at the table in any discussions shaping its future, amid an ongoing debate over how the continent should respond to US-led efforts to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine with Russia. FRANCE 24's Europe Editor Armen Georgian tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Australia: Teen found alive after six days missing in bush
stories.description: A 17-year-old Australian has been found alive and well after spending six days missing in bushland east of Melbourne. After being spotted by helicopter, the teen was winched to safety before an emotional reunion with his mother who joked that “he’s never leaving the house again”.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: For the love of French butter: 'Le beurre' spreading joy globally
stories.description: French butter is having a moment! We dive into France's love of butter, the many rules that apply to "le beurre", how tourists are hauling back flavoured artisan butter as souvenirs, and how the French language has embraced many a butter expression over the years.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Armed robbers flee Paris De Beers store on motorcycles after jewellery heist
stories.description: Four black-clad individuals sped away from De Beers jeweller in Paris's second arrondissement Thursday morning after stealing hundreds of thousands of euros worth of luxury goods at gunpoint. Police are searching for those responsible.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: ICRC 'currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France's social safety net: Can it afford to be so generous?
stories.description: Created in the aftermath of World War II, France's social security system has become one of the pillars of French society, providing everything from healthcare and family benefits to pensions. But with an ageing population and mounting deficits, this ambitious model is facing a major financial test. We look at how the system works, why it is so deeply valued by the French and whether the country can afford to keep its promise of protecting everyone – from cradle to grave.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ICRC 'currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed. Spoljaric warns that the international rules established to protect civilians are being progressively weakened amid proliferating armed conflicts, technological transformations and the retreat of diplomacy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mississippi elects its first African American to US Senate since Reconstruction
stories.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black US Senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory, confirmed on November 11 after prolonged ballot counting, marks a major political shift in the conservative state. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
stories.description: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
stories.description: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Rare pictures from Marilyn Monroe's final shoot on auction in Paris
stories.description: Prints from the personal collection of photographer Bert Stern are going under the hammer in Paris on December 2, marking the first time his private archive has been offered for sale. Among the highlights of the auction are iconic photographs of Marilyn Monroe, taken just weeks before her death.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Paraguayans get some savings back after banking collapse disrupted economy
stories.description: Paraguay's Central Bank said Wednesday, November 11, it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors locked out of their accounts when it collapsed last week. The digital bank's takeover on November 3 triggered massive protests across Paraguay and led to the impeachment and arrest of ex-president Santiago Pena, who is linked to Ueno.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: European leaders gather in Dublin to discuss Ukraine's security, and their own
stories.description: Leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday, November 12, for a summit focused on the continent’s fragile security, amid a new US-backed effort to revive talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war. The meeting of the European Political Community brought together heads of state and government from European countries and the UK, as well as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: New York: Deadly building collapse in Brooklyn
stories.description: A three-storey building collapsed in New York’s Brooklyn on Wednesday, killing at least two and injuring 17 others. The building, in the Flatbush area, collapsed at around 4pm local time, and tumbled into a neighbouring construction site, with the cause of the collapse still under investigation.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Thousands of schools evacuated in Italy as bomb threats spread across Europe
stories.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts across Europe in recent weeks, which have prompted growing concern about the possibility of an escalation in hybrid warfare.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: COP31: Climate disruption puts farmers and global food supplies under pressure
stories.description: As delegates gather in Turkey for the COP31 climate conference, discussions are focusing on emissions and climate targets. But humanitarian agencies are highlighting another urgent consequence of climate disruption: growing food insecurity. With the return of El Niño adding to concerns over extreme weather and its impact on food production, the Food and Agriculture Organisation is calling for food systems to be placed at the heart of climate action.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Nvidia board weighing up whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang
stories.description: Nvidia's board is holding a late-night meeting to decide whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang after a second extramarital affair was revealed. The scandal has revealed a major weakness at the heart of the chipmaker sitting at the heart of the AI boom: the lack of a clear succession plan. We take a closer look.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: DR Congo's Tshisekedi signs referendum law amid fears of third-term bid
stories.description: DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi paved the way for a constitutional amendment on November 10 by signing a law authorising a referendum. The move comes amid concerns that he could seek a third term in office, with opposition figures accusing him of manoeuvring to remain in power.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Scott Colom makes history in Mississippi as first Black senator in more than 140 years
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 12: We look at reactions from Spain after the country's first nationwide general strike in 14 years. It comes two weeks before snap general elections. Also: Scott Colom makes history as the first Black senator in Mississippi in 145 years after an epic Senate midterm race finally concluded. Finally, fans of Barça will be able to inter their ashes at Camp Nou as part of a new offer by the club to allow supporters to cheer on the team in the afterlife.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, 42-day countdown to 'Ebola-free' begins
stories.description: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, who has now officially recovered. The 11 other people who had been in quarantine were also released from hospital on Wednesday, November 11, as the country began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free. FRANCE 24's Nairobi correspondent Bastien Renouil reports.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: COP31: Experts call for zero waste, as Africa grapples with mounting garbage
stories.description: As the COP31 climate summit gets under way this week in Turkey, experts are calling for zero-waste solutions to tackle Africa's growing waste crisis. As governments search for ways to address the crisis, a new report warns of a growing push for waste-to-energy incineration across the continent. FRANCE 24 spoke to Mponwe Minette, founder and executive director of Soft Power Global and a climate activist.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom flips US Senate seat in stunning upset
stories.description: In a historic upset, Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks projected Wednesday, making him the first African American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years. Report by Morgan Ayre
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years as anger over housing leads to clashes
stories.description: A general strike by 4 million Spanish workers — around one-fifth of the total workforce — against the country's housing crisis was mostly peaceful on Wednesday, unions said, though by the evening clashes erupted in some areas of Barcelona and Madrid. It is ‌the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Peruvian pope' makes jubilant return to his second 'homeland'
stories.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in his "beloved" Peru on Wednesday, a nostalgic return to the nation where he spent two decades as a missionary before being tapped to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. The 71-year-old pontiff landed in Lima on the last leg of an arduous three-nation Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Who is Jensen Huang? Nvidia chief under scrutiny over affair and spying reports
stories.description: Nvidia's board is meeting to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, as the AI chip giant grapples with reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. Huang's future is now in the balance at the company he co-founded and helped transform into a global AI powerhouse. We look back at his rise and his journey to becoming one of the most influential figures in the AI industry.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Colom as state's first post-Civil War Black senator
stories.description: Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday in Mississippi's closely contested US Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black US senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction. Colom's narrow victory is a seismic shift in Mississippi, which has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations despite having the largest share of Black residents of any US state.

stories.title: Two dead, several injured after New York building collapses
stories.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people who firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws.

stories.title: Hybrid warfare: Hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, UK in latest disruption
stories.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats. Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain, Scotland and Ireland. The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts in recent weeks including on flights across Europe and cyber attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries, including Italy. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

stories.title: Kylian Mbappé to miss Thursday's Nations League clash against Italy
stories.description: It's a major blow for France. Coach Zinédine Zidane will have to do without his captain, Kylian Mbappé, this Thursday as Les Bleus take on Italy in the Nations League. The Real Madrid forward is suffering from minor hamstring discomfort but could return for Sunday's clash against Turkey. In the meantime, Zidane has decided to call up Senny Mayulu for his first senior international appearance.

stories.description: Should we be worried about cyberattacks targeting everyday household appliances, from smart vacuums to washing machines and food processors? The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity has warned that these connected devices could become vulnerable to hacking, prompting experts to call for greater investment in cybersecurity to address emerging threats.

stories.description: Millions of workers in Spain shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, as part of the country's first general strike in 14 years. Following a peaceful march in Barcelona over soaring rents and property prices, and the rising cost of living, protesters smashed storefronts, set off small bonfires, burned bins and launched fireworks towards police. The unrest comes just weeks before snap elections, called by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

At the heart of the Dec. 2 auction is The Last Sitting, a series of photographs taken in June and July 1962 at the Hotel Bel-Air in Los Angeles, just weeks before Monroe's death. Those close to him, as well as his fellow sports journalists have campaigned tirelessly for his release with the affair even attracting the attention of Zinedine Zidane, manager of the French football team. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Thibault Bruttin, Director General of Reporters Without Borders. He says that Gleizes has probably become "a token in a diplomatic game that we don't totally understand, that we don't totally master, up to the point where we are asking ourselves 'has he become a state hostage?'".

Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation. Braving heavy rain, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting "We have no home" as they called for more affordable housing. China accused of exploiting a vulnerability at the heart of the Silicon Valley giant that reigns supreme over two-thirds of the planet’s AI computing power production, the Nvidia co-founder tempted by the flesh. stories.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
stories.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge. "The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention." For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender. The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens. "Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them." Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns. "People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election." Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.

The withdrawal of Israeli forces from Hebron has not brought an end to the humanitarian crisis. According to Venturi, some 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced, 15 houses were reportedly demolished, and continuing restrictions on movement have obstructed access to essential healthcare. "Those families whose houses were demolished have nowhere to go back to." Venturi describes how the "movement restrictions during the lockdown prevented medical teams from reaching communities." Hospitals are also reporting shortages of essential medicines.

stories.title: 'Europe not going anywhere': G7 summit a 'signal to Russians' that Europe is standing behind Ukraine
